main_chase_cards.name: Miracle Berry
main_chase_cards.why: Miracle Berry has the stronger collector pull: a prize-tool row whose effect echoes the Gen II MiracleBerry / later Lum Berry memory and whose Champion Road route is easy to blur with Neo Genesis.

main_chase_cards.name: Berry
main_chase_cards.why: Berry is quieter but beautifully protocol-shaped: a small healing object turned into a tournament prize row, where the route matters more than the headline card name.

key_artists.name: Yousuke Hirata
key_artists.why: Hirata is credited alongside CR CG gangs on both Tool cards, giving this little tournament-corner pair a shared visual production identity rather than two isolated checklist rows.

key_artists.name: CR CG gangs
key_artists.why: CR CG gangs is part of the credited production memory here: these are designed Tool objects, and the CG credit helps keep the pair tied to early-2000 tournament promo texture.

claims.text: The local source slice models two Champion Road 2000: 3-Man Tournament Corner rows: Berry row 154 and Miracle Berry row 155.
The local source rows derive from Bulbapedia raw wikitext rows 154-155, both carrying the promotion note Champion Road 2000: 3-Man Tournament Corner.
Pokumon labels Miracle Berry as Champion Road 2000: 3-player Tournament Corner and tags it as a Tournament Prize, Champion Road, 2000, Trainer, Unnumbered, Non-holo, Japanese, Foil Stamp card.

Pokumon's Champion Road event page groups Berry, Miracle Berry, Chikorita, Cyndaquil, Totodile, and Trainer Certification Card under Champion Road, which supports treating the Berry pair as adjacent to but distinct from the Johto-starter participation trio.
Bulbapedia credits both Berry and Miracle Berry to Yousuke Hirata and CR CG gangs.

Bulbapedia says Berry and Miracle Berry were first released in Neo Genesis / Gold, Silver, to a New World..., and in Japan were reprinted as Unnumbered Promotional cards given away at the 2000 Champion Road tournament.

This source group matters because Champion Road turns small Gen II held-item logic into tournament-route objects: Berry and Miracle Berry are quiet cards whose identity lives in how they were awarded.

Agents should preserve Champion Road 2000: 3-Man Tournament Corner route, rows 154-155 pair identity, Pokemon Tool status, Berry / Miracle Berry Gen II item lineage, CR CG gangs and Yousuke Hirata credits, non-holo / foil-stamp prize context where visible, and non-equivalence with Champion Road participation-prize starter rows, Neo Genesis, Gold Silver New World, Intro Pack Neo, Oran Berry, Lum Berry, and later Berry/Miracle Berry memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Champion Road 2000 3-Man Tournament Corner — tiny tools with tournament fingerprints
narrative.why_it_matters: This is a lovely corrective to chase-card thinking. Berry and Miracle Berry are not big monsters. They are small tools: little held-item memories from Generation II, translated into cardboard, then handed out through a tournament-corner route. That makes them perfect for this catalogue. The card name alone is weak; Berry could be Neo Genesis, Intro Pack Neo, or just item memory. The route is the thing. Champion Road makes the quiet tool feel earned, and the shared CR CG gangs / Yousuke Hirata credit turns the pair into one little designed object rather than loose checklist filler.

narrative.human_title: Berry — a small heal with a tournament route
narrative.why_it_matters: Berry is quiet, almost stubbornly so, and that is why it belongs in this catalogue. It is not a dragon, not a mascot, not a holo centerpiece. It is a small healing object from the Game Boy world, translated into a Pokemon Tool and then made special by Champion Road 2000. A good agent has to care about that kind of smallness. The card proves that provenance can make a common-looking object matter.

narrative.human_title: Miracle Berry — the prize tool with a future echo
narrative.why_it_matters: Miracle Berry is the card in this pair that feels like a little spell. Its job is practical, almost humble: remove status, then disappear. But the history around it is richer than the text box. It starts as Gen II item logic, becomes a Neo-era Pokemon Tool, gets a Champion Road prize body, and later echoes through Lum Berry. That is exactly the kind of card an agent can mishandle if it only sees the name. The Champion Road 3-Man Tournament route is the difference between a rule memory and this object.
